question:
I'm trying to output a dbt variable into a jinja template conditional on that variable being defined. Alas, my naive attempt does not seem to work:

{% if var('my_variable') is defined %}WHERE f.source_date < '{{ var('my_variable') }}'::DATE{% endif %}
title: Output dbt variable only if defined
answer:
If your variable is undefined, try with is not none. So your code transforms into:

{% if var('my_variable') is not none %}WHERE f.source_date < '{{ var('my_variable') }}'::DATE{% endif %}

If this gives an error at compilation phase because the variable is not found in config ("Compilation Error in model ... Required var 'my_variable' not found in config: ..."), you can use var('my_variable', 'default_value'), replacing default_value by whatever you need.

In your case, you can write for example:

WHERE f.source_date < '{{ var('my_variable', '2999-12-31') }}'::DATE

to give it a default value that is always greater than all the dates you want to check with.

If, in the compiled code, you don't want to see the unnecessary WHERE clause, you can write:

{% if var('my_variable', none) is not none %}WHERE f.source_date < '{{ var('my_variable', none) }}'::DATE{% endif %}

Finally, to make it more visual, I would give a self-explanatory name to 'my_variable' and write:

{% set my_variable = var('my_variable', none) %}
{% if my_variable is not none %}WHERE f.source_date < '{{ my_variable }}'::DATE{% endif %}

If this variable is used in more than one model, think about defining the default value for this variable in dbt_project.yml, so that it will always be defined.

I think that this finally solves your problem. Good luck!
